Finally, I write an answer sentence.

u01l01.objective: I can build a number using place value.
u01l01.situation: The class gathers 246 seeds to prepare small bags. How can they be counted quickly?
u01l01.discover: Ten units make a ten; ten tens make a hundred. In 246, the 2 is worth 200, the 4 is worth 40 and the 6 is worth 6.

manipulate.title: Build the number 324
manipulate.instruction: Build 324 using hundred blocks, ten sticks and single units.
manipulate.hint: Start with the hundreds: how many hundred blocks are needed?
manipulate.strongHint: 324 is 3 hundred blocks, 2 ten sticks and 4 units. Adjust each counter one at a time.

example.medium: Intermediate. What number is made of 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 units?
example.reflection: Reflection. In 609, what is the value of the digit 6?

practice.title: Break down 572
practice.instruction: Build 572 with blocks, sticks and units, just like in the guided example.
practice.hint: Look at each digit of 572: hundreds, then tens, then units.

reflect.title: Which number is it?
reflect.instruction: Work out the number from its breakdown, then write it in digits.
reflect.hint: Add the hundreds first, then the tens, then the units.
reflect.strongHint: 8 hundreds make 800, 3 tens make 30, and there are 5 units left: 800 + 30 + 5.
reflect.prompt: What number is made of 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 units?

play.title: Deliver to the right depot
play.instruction: Deliver the hundreds, tens and units of 463 to the right depot by building the number.
play.hint: Place the hundred blocks first, then the ten sticks, then the units.
play.strongHint: 463 is 4 hundred blocks, 6 ten sticks and 3 units.

u01l01.remember: Ten units make a ten; ten tens make a hundred.

check.title: What is the highlighted digit worth?
check.instruction: Choose the exact value of the hundreds digit in 609.
check.hint: This digit sits in the hundreds place: it isn't just worth itself.
check.strongHint: In 609, the 6 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 600.
check.prompt: In 609, what is the value of the digit 6?

u01l02.objective: I can move from words to digits.
u01l02.situation: A card reads "four hundred and thirty-two" drawn bags.
u01l02.discover: We spot the hundreds, then the tens and the units. An empty place is written with 0: six hundred and five is written 605.

manipulate.title: Listen and build
manipulate.instruction: Build each number you are given, with blocks, sticks and units: 407, then 760, then 999.
manipulate.hint: An empty place is written with 0: don't add a ten stick if there isn't one.
manipulate.strongHint: 407 = 4 hundreds, 0 tens, 7 units. Check each number digit by digit.

example.easy: Easy. Write in digits: three hundred and twenty-eight.
example.reflection: Reflection. Write the number made of 5 hundreds and 7 units.

practice.title: Words and digits
practice.instruction: Match each number to its correct word form, or each word form to its number.
practice.hint: Spot the hundreds first, in the words or in the digits.
practice.strongHint: Three hundred and twenty-eight = 3 hundreds, 2 tens and 8 units, so 328.

reflect.title: Find the number
reflect.instruction: Work out the number from its breakdown, then write it in digits.
reflect.hint: 5 hundreds and 7 units: there is no ten, so 0 tens.
reflect.prompt: Write the number made of 5 hundreds and 7 units.

play.title: Match the number card
play.instruction: Match each word form to its number card, or each number card to its word form.
play.hint: Count the hundreds in the word form before choosing.
play.strongHint: Read the number digit by digit: hundreds, then tens, then units.

u01l02.remember: We spot the hundreds, then the tens and the units.

check.title: Build the announced number
check.instruction: Build 693 with blocks, sticks and units.
check.hint: 693: how many hundreds, tens and units?

u01l03.situation: Two storehouses show 487 and 509 bags. Which one has more?
u01l03.discover: We compare the hundreds first, then the tens, then the units.

manipulate.title: Build, then compare
manipulate.instruction: Build 438, then 483, and look at the first place where they differ.
manipulate.hint: The hundreds are the same: look at the tens.
manipulate.strongHint: 438 has 3 tens, 483 has 8 tens: so 483 is bigger.

example.reflection: Reflection. Find two numbers between 495 and 500.

practice.title: Compare the numbers
practice.instruction: Choose the symbol that correctly compares each pair of numbers.
practice.hint: Compare the hundreds digit of each number first.
practice.strongHint: If the hundreds are equal, compare the tens, then the units.

reflect.title: Order the numbers
reflect.instruction: Place the four numbers from smallest to largest.
reflect.hint: Start by spotting the smallest hundreds digit.
reflect.strongHint: 132 has 1 hundred, 213 has 2, 312 and 321 have 3: compare their tens next.

play.title: The canoe race
play.instruction: Move forward the canoe carrying the bigger number in each round.
play.hint: Look at the hundreds of each number first.
play.strongHint: Compare hundreds, then tens, then units to find the bigger number.

u01l03.remember: We compare the hundreds first, then the tens, then the units.

check.title: Find a hidden number
check.instruction: Write a whole number that is strictly between the two limits.
check.hint: 495 and 500 don't count: look for a number in between.
check.strongHint: Between 495 and 500, you can choose 496, 497, 498 or 499.

u01l04.objective: I can spot a pattern and estimate.
u01l04.situation: The markers along a path show 200, 250, 300, then one sign is missing.
u01l04.discover: A pattern moves forward following a rule. To round to the nearest ten, we choose the closest ten.

manipulate.title: Continue the pattern
manipulate.instruction: Continue the pattern counting up by 25 using place-value cards.
manipulate.hint: Look at how much the pattern moves forward each time.
manipulate.strongHint: The pattern moves forward by 50 each time: 200, 250, 300, then 350.

example.medium: Intermediate. Round 63 to the nearest ten.

practice.title: Complete the pattern
practice.instruction: Find the missing number in the pattern.
practice.hint: Look at the gap between the numbers you already know.
practice.strongHint: The pattern moves forward by 10 each time: after 350 comes 360.

reflect.title: Round to the nearest ten
reflect.instruction: Choose the ten closest to the given number.
reflect.hint: Look at the units digit: is it closer to 0 or to 10?
reflect.strongHint: 63 is closer to 60 than to 70, because 3 is closer to 0 than to 10.

play.title: Repair the number path
play.instruction: Repair the path by finding the missing number in the pattern.
play.hint: Compare the two known numbers to find the pattern's step.
play.strongHint: The path moves forward by 100 each time: after 600 comes 700.

u01l04.remember: A pattern moves forward following a rule.

check.title: Discover the rule
check.instruction: Choose the step that explains this number pattern.
check.hint: Work out the gap between two neighbouring numbers in the pattern.

u01eval.intro: Work on your own first. Use a drawing if you need to, and explain at least one answer.

q1.title: Question 1
q1.instruction: Work out the number from its breakdown.
q1.hint: Add the hundreds, the tens, then the units.
q1.strongHint: 8 hundreds make 800, 3 tens make 30, and there are 5 units left: 800 + 30 + 5.
q1.prompt: What number is made of 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 units?

q2.title: Question 2
q2.instruction: Choose the word form that matches the number shown exactly.
q2.hint: Spot the hundreds first: nine hundred.
q2.strongHint: 904 = nine hundred and four: there are no tens.

q3.title: Question 3
q3.instruction: Place the four numbers from smallest to largest.
q3.hint: Compare the hundreds digit of each number first.
q3.strongHint: 132 has 1 hundred, 213 has 2, 312 and 321 have 3: compare their tens next.

q4.title: Question 4
q4.instruction: Choose the ten closest to the given number.
q4.hint: Look at the units digit: is it closer to 0 or to 10?
